title.justification: The paper focuses on an empirical study regarding the impact of smaller batch sizes on the performance of deep reinforcement learning agents, particularly in value-based settings.
title.quote: In this work we present a broad empirical study that suggests reducing the batch size can result in a number of significant performance gains; this is surprising, as the general tendency when training neural networks is towards larger batch sizes for improved performance.

extractions.description: This paper explores how varying the batch size affects performance in online value-based deep reinforcement learning (RL). It presents empirical evidence that smaller batch sizes may significantly improve agent performance across different RL agents and architectures. The authors investigated this effect with comprehensive analyses of batch sizes' impact on exploration, computational cost, and network dynamics, and conclude that reduced batch sizes often lead to better sample efficiency and faster computational times. Furthermore, the findings point towards potential general improvements in network expressivity and plasticity.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: Although the paper has implications for computational efficiency which could indirectly relate to energy efficiency and sustainability, the central focus of the research is on deep reinforcement learning methodology rather than direct climate or ecological sustainability applications.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: Broader impact Although the work presented here is mostly of an academic nature, it aids in the development of more capable autonomous agents. While our contributions do not directly contribute to any negative societal impacts, we urge the community to consider these when building on our research.

primary_category.justification: The study is primarily about improving computational methodologies in reinforcement learning, not directly related to any specific category or sub-category in Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development.
primary_category.quote: Our work has broader implications than just the choice of the batch size hyper-parameter. For instance, our findings on the impact of variance on performance suggest a promising avenue for new algorithmic innovations via the explicit injection of variance.

secondary_categories.justification: The potential reduction in computational requirements mentioned in the paper can be associated with reduced energy consumption, which is related to Climate Change Mitigation.
secondary_categories.quote: Considering the unsuitable increase in computational requirements, progress with deep learning demands more compute-efficient training methods. A natural direction is to eliminate algorithmic inefficiencies in the learning process, aiming to reduce time, energy consumption and carbon footprint associated with training these models.

primary_sub_category.justification: The research does not directly address a specific sub-category within Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development.
primary_sub_category.quote: Beyond the obvious performance and wall-time gains we observe, changing the batch size appears to have knock-on effects on exploration as well as asymptotic behaviour.

secondary_sub_categories.justification: The mention of efforts to reduce computational energy consumption aligns with aims to improve energy efficiency, albeit the paper is focused on algorithmic improvements rather than building-specific technologies.
secondary_sub_categories.quote: A natural direction is to eliminate algorithmic inefficiencies in the learning process, aiming to reduce time, energy consumption and carbon footprint associated with training these models.

new_primary_category.justification: The paper's findings are methodological within the realm of machine learning and computational techniques, not directly introducing a new area within Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development.
new_primary_category.quote: Our findings here suggest the opposite: the batch size parameter generally alters the agent’s learning curves in surprising ways, and reducing the batch size below its standard value is often beneficial.
